pages.title: Page 1
pages.text: I am writing this beside the tree, because the tree is where it started. The lights went out one at a time, and nobody looked up. Please look up. Keep your light on the things that hide and they will stop being able to hide. The next page is where the choir keeps the winter out.

pages.title: Page 2
pages.text: The choir hums one low note all night now. Join in and it stops. Do not, and it comes closer, a little each verse. Be careful of the woman who bakes too kindly. A cookie left on the doorstep is not a gift. It is a bill. Somewhere the lanes still glow warm, where pins fall like thunder.

pages.title: Page 3
pages.text: Here the lights are still on, and I think it is because people here still laugh. Rest. Drink something hot. The ones outside cannot cross this door, but they can wait, and they are patient. On a night near the middle of the month she will come looking for what was baked. Look for the bridge next.

pages.title: Page 4
pages.text: Under the bridge the water keeps every name it has ever heard. Say yours quietly. Somewhere beneath the old stones there is a trapdoor, and something under it has been practising your voice. If you hear yourself calling from the dark, do not answer. Answer the camp instead, up where the tents are.

pages.title: Page 5
pages.text: Stand still too long on the high ground and a large eye opens in the sky. It does not blink. It does not need to. Keep moving and keep to the light, and it loses interest. The old stone on the mountain above Feda knows more than I do. Find it before the snow does.

pages.title: Page 6
pages.text: The great stone was not left here by the ice. It was set down, carefully, and then it was told to wait. Put your hand on it and you will feel it counting. Past the bridge at Feda the sky comes close, round and bright. Look for the globe.

pages.title: Page 7
pages.text: Something with wings and a long cold breath has been circling the top of the world. It is waiting for the snow to grow deep enough to hide the shape of its shadow. It is old and it is not cruel, but it is very hungry. Climb to the cairn above the town. The wind there is a teacher.

pages.title: Page 8
pages.text: These stones are not trail markers. They are a tally. Each one is somebody who stopped walking and decided to stay. There are more cairns than there should be, and they have begun to lean toward the town. Follow the water downhill, along the great pipe, to where it begins.

pages.title: Page 9
pages.text: Water drops two hundred metres through that pipe and still arrives afraid. Under the old power station is a hatch with no handle on the outside. Do not open it alone, and do not open it twice. Down by the fjord, a machine hums that was never meant to hum. Go and listen.

pages.title: Page 10
pages.text: This hum is not electricity. It is something breathing through the wires, and the red sky is borrowing its breath. If the hum ever stops, run toward any light you can see. Lamps are kind. Lamps are the only kind thing left. Go home next, to the house with the cellar nobody mentions.

pages.title: Page 11
pages.text: There is a cellar door in this house that you have walked past a thousand times. It is warm to the touch. Do not knock. It will knock when it is ready, and it will know which of you to ask for. The last page is up high, where the town's biggest window faces the tree.

pages.title: Page 12
pages.text: You found them all, so you are the one I wrote them for. Christmas Eve will come whether the lights return or not. Gather your light, your friend, and your nerve. When the last night comes, be at the tree before the bells, and bring everything that glows.
